title: From Memory-Hungry HNSW to Quantized SPANN: The Technical Evolution of Pinterest's Manas Platform
gist: Pinterest re-engineered its Manas search platform — 80 clusters serving Home Feed, Search, Related Pins, Ads and Notifications over tens of billions of embeddings — by replacing memory-resident HNSW with scalar/product quantization and SSD-backed SPANN, cutting production serving costs 20-30% and CPU time by over 40% on a 5-billion-embedding workload. It is now piloting multi-vector ColBERT-style late interaction retrieval to get past the expressiveness ceiling of single-vector two-tower models.

themes.theme: Vector search economics at billion scale

insights.claim: Pinterest runs its Manas vector search platform across 80 clusters over tens of billions of embeddings, powering Home Feed, Search, Related Pins, Ads and Notifications — making retrieval infrastructure a shared dependency of both engagement and monetization surfaces.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Retrieval cost is a direct input to ad-serving gross margin at consumer-scale platforms; efficiency gains here fall straight to contribution margin.
insights.locator: Pinterest Engineering evolved its distributed search platform

insights.claim: Standard memory-resident HNSW becomes economically untenable as corpora scale into billions of items, creating mounting cost, hardware allocation and infrastructure-flexibility constraints that force a move off pure RAM-based indexes.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: RAM is the binding cost in large-scale vector search — a demand signal for SSD/IOPS-optimized serving and a headwind for memory-priced vector-DB pricing models.
insights.quote: traditional memory-hungry vector search algorithms like standard HNSW face mounting cost, hardware allocation, and infrastructure flexibility challenges
insights.locator: As the underlying corpus scales rapidly into billions of items

insights.claim: Quantization delivered 20-30% serving cost savings across Pinterest's production workloads once scalar and product quantization were launched online.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: A 20-30% cut in serving cost from a purely algorithmic change sets the benchmark any vector-infrastructure vendor must beat to justify a contract.
insights.quote: Online experiments successfully launched SQ and PQ, realizing 20–30% serving cost savings across production workloads.
insights.locator: Online experiments successfully launched SQ and PQ

insights.claim: On a 100-million-embedding GraphSage dataset, product quantization shrank HNSW indices by 74% and inverted-file indices by 93% but dropped recall to a 70-80% range, while scalar quantization shrank them 59% and 75% respectively while holding recall above 90%.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: The compression-vs-recall frontier is quantified: PQ buys footprint at a real quality cost, SQ is the safer default for quality-sensitive surfaces.
insights.locator: the Pinterest team implemented Scalar Quantization (SQ) and Product Quantization (PQ)

insights.claim: IVF plus scalar quantization outperformed the uncompressed HNSW baseline on both axes in Pinterest's offline benchmark — 25 GB index at 95.71% Recall@100 and 1588.8 QPS versus 121 GB at 93.72% and 302.5 QPS — meaning the graph-based index was not on the efficient frontier for this workload.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: HNSW's default status in the vector-database industry is challenged by a 5x-throughput, 5x-smaller alternative — reason to question vendor benchmarks built on HNSW.
insights.locator: Using IVF plus SQ yields a 25 GB index size

insights.claim: IVF plus product quantization compressed a 97 GB baseline index to 6.8 GB — a roughly 14x reduction — while raising throughput to 1747.9 QPS, at the cost of Recall@100 falling from 91.69% to 76.00%.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: For candidate-generation stages where downstream ranking can recover quality, extreme compression is nearly free — a template for tiered retrieval cost design.
insights.locator: Applying IVF plus PQ compresses the index down to 6.8 GB

insights.claim: Lower-bit vector representations normally require a decode step before distance computation, creating a CPU bottleneck that Pinterest removed with a Linear Scaling SQ implementation using SIMD intrinsics, cutting query compute resources a further 10-15%.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Memory savings from quantization can be silently offset by CPU cost unless SIMD-level work is done — a hidden diligence question for vector-DB claims.
insights.locator: Shifting to lower-bit representations normally requires a decoding step

insights.claim: In Pinterest's head-to-head evaluation, SPANN combined with product quantization achieved 3x the QPS of DiskANN at one-third the latency, with only about a 5% recall drop.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: DiskANN is the more widely adopted disk-based ANN algorithm; a 3x/3x gap for SPANN is a concrete reason to re-examine infrastructure built on it.
insights.quote: SPANN combined with PQ achieved 3x the QPS of DiskANN with 1/3 the latency and only a minor 5% recall drop
insights.locator: To further cut RAM costs by moving index storage to high-throughput SSDs

insights.claim: Pinterest's custom SPANN architecture keeps only a small fast centroid index in memory to locate partitions while storing large posting lists on SSD, converting a RAM-capacity problem into an IOPS-optimization problem.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Shifting the bottleneck from DRAM to SSD IOPS changes the hardware mix large platforms buy — relevant to memory versus NAND demand assumptions.
insights.locator: The custom SPANN architecture keeps a small, fast centroid index in memory

insights.claim: On a Pin recommendation workload indexing over 5 billion embeddings, SPANN saved more than 40% of CPU time for production queries compared with fully in-memory HNSW.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Moving indexes to SSD cut compute as well as memory, breaking the usual assumption that disk-based serving trades CPU for RAM.
insights.quote: SPANN saved over 40% of CPU time for production queries compared to full in-memory HNSW
insights.locator: In a Pin recommendation evaluation indexing over 5 billion embeddings

insights.claim: Pinterest is moving from single-vector two-tower retrieval to multi-vector late interaction models such as ColBERT with Sum of MaxSim scoring, explicitly to escape the expressiveness limits of collapsing a query into one embedding.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: If the largest recommender operators abandon two-tower single-vector retrieval, vector databases optimized for one-vector-per-document lookups face an architectural refresh cycle.
insights.quote: To move past the expressiveness limits of single-vector two-tower models
insights.locator: To move past the expressiveness limits

insights.claim: Supporting late interaction forced Manas changes beyond the model layer: the query parser had to split multi-token queries into multiple embeddings and execute simultaneous ANN searches across indices.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Multi-vector retrieval multiplies per-query index lookups, partially reversing the cost savings from quantization — watch the net serving-cost trajectory.
insights.locator: Implementing this in Manas required updating the query parser

insights.claim: The multi-embedding query capability is only at pilot stage with a single internal client team in live production, so the late interaction shift is unproven at Pinterest scale.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Separates shipped savings (quantization, SPANN) from aspirational roadmap (ColBERT) when judging how durable the efficiency gains are.
insights.quote: A successful pilot launch is currently underway with an internal client team
insights.locator: A successful pilot launch is currently underway
